objects.description: C++ deleter functor usable with std::unique_ptr<void, MEM_freeN_smart_ptr_deleter> to free memory via MEM_freeN and null the pointer.

functions.name: MEM_freeN
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated by the C-style MEM_* allocation functions in this module. Do not use for memory created with MEM_new or C++ new/delete wrappers.
requirements: vmemh must either be a pointer previously returned by this module’s C-style allocation functions (e.g., MEM_mallocN, MEM_callocN, MEM_reallocN_id, etc.) or NULL.
It is illegal to pass a pointer allocated by MEM_new or other C++ new/delete wrappers from this module.
Passing NULL is safe and has no effect.

functions.name: MEM_freeN
functions.description: Type-safe C-style free for objects allocated without invoking constructors (e.g., via MEM_mallocN<T>/MEM_callocN<T>). Only for trivial types.
requirements: On MSVC: T must be trivially destructible. On other compilers: T must be trivially copyable and trivially destructible (is_trivial_after_construction).
ptr must have been allocated with the C-style MEM_* allocation functions (type-safe wrappers or untyped).
Do not use for objects allocated with MEM_new or requiring a destructor.

functions.name: MEM_dupallocN
functions.description: Duplicates a previously allocated memory block and returns a pointer to a newly allocated copy. NULL-safe (returns NULL if vmemh is NULL).
requirements: vmemh should be a pointer previously allocated by this module’s C-style allocation functions; behavior is undefined for foreign pointers.
May be called with NULL, in which case it returns NULL.
Caller must free the returned pointer with MEM_freeN.

functions.name: MEM_dupallocN
functions.signature: template <typename T> T *MEM_dupallocN(const char *allocation_name, const T &other);
functions.description: Allocates storage for a T and duplicates the contents of other via memcpy. A type-safe alternative to the untyped MEM_dupallocN for trivial types.
requirements: On MSVC: T must be trivially assignable and trivially destructible. On other compilers: T must be trivially copyable and trivially destructible (is_trivial_after_construction).
allocation_name is a tag/name for tracking; recommended to be a static string.
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN.
Only appropriate for trivial types; for non-trivial types use MEM_new.

functions.name: MEM_reallocN_id
functions.signature: extern void *(*MEM_reallocN_id)(void *vmemh, size_t len, const char *str);
functions.description: Function-pointer entry for reallocation. Reallocates a block to a new size and frees the old block; implemented as allocate+copy+free rather than an optimized in-place realloc.
requirements: vmemh should be a pointer previously allocated by this module’s C-style allocation functions.
len is the new size in bytes.
str is a tag/name used for allocation tracking (usage semantics are module-specific).
Returns a new pointer which must be freed with MEM_freeN; the old pointer is considered freed regardless of success semantics of the implementation.

functions.name: MEM_recallocN_id
functions.signature: extern void *(*MEM_recallocN_id)(void *vmemh, size_t len, const char *str);
functions.description: Function-pointer entry for reallocation that zero-initializes any newly added bytes beyond the previous size.
requirements: vmemh should be a pointer previously allocated by this module’s C-style allocation functions.
len is the new size in bytes.
str is a tag/name used for allocation tracking.
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN.

functions.name: MEM_callocN
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized memory of size len bytes with a tracking tag/name str.
requirements: len is the number of bytes to allocate (may be zero-size per platform semantics).
str must be a static string (only a pointer is stored).
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN.
Do not free with MEM_delete.

functions.name: MEM_callocN
functions.description: Type-safe wrapper that allocates zero-initialized storage for a single T without invoking its constructor. Only for trivial types.
requirements: On MSVC: T must be trivially constructible. On other compilers: T must be trivial.
allocation_name is a tag/name for tracking; recommended to be a static string.
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN (not MEM_delete).

functions.name: MEM_calloc_arrayN
functions.signature: void *MEM_calloc_arrayN(size_t len, size_t size, const char *str);
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized memory for an array of len elements of element size size, with overflow checking, and tags the allocation with str.
requirements: The product len * size must fit in size_t; the function aborts on overflow.
str must be a static string (only a pointer is stored).
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN.
Do not free with MEM_delete.

functions.name: MEM_calloc_arrayN
functions.signature: template <typename T> T *MEM_calloc_arrayN(const size_t length, const char *allocation_name);
functions.description: Type-safe wrapper that allocates zero-initialized storage for an array of length elements of type T without invoking constructors. Only for trivial types.
requirements: On MSVC: T must be trivially constructible. On other compilers: T must be trivial.
length is the number of elements to allocate.
allocation_name is a tag/name for tracking; recommended to be a static string.
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN.

functions.name: MEM_mallocN
functions.description: Allocates uninitialized memory of size len bytes with a tracking tag/name str.
requirements: len is the number of bytes to allocate.
str must be a static string (only a pointer is stored).
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN.
Do not free with MEM_delete.

functions.name: MEM_mallocN
functions.description: Type-safe wrapper that allocates uninitialized storage for a single T without invoking its constructor. Only for trivial types.
requirements: On MSVC: T must be trivially constructible. On other compilers: T must be trivial.
allocation_name is a tag/name for tracking; recommended to be a static string.
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN.

functions.name: MEM_malloc_arrayN
functions.signature: void *MEM_malloc_arrayN(size_t len, size_t size, const char *str);
functions.description: Allocates uninitialized memory for an array of len elements of element size size with overflow checking, tagged with str.
requirements: The product len * size must fit in size_t; the function aborts on overflow.
str must be a static string (only a pointer is stored).
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN.
Do not free with MEM_delete.

functions.name: MEM_malloc_arrayN
functions.signature: template <typename T> T *MEM_malloc_arrayN(const size_t length, const char *allocation_name);
functions.description: Type-safe wrapper that allocates uninitialized storage for an array of length elements of type T without invoking constructors. Only for trivial types.
requirements: On MSVC: T must be trivially constructible. On other compilers: T must be trivial.
length is the number of elements to allocate.
allocation_name is a tag/name for tracking; recommended to be a static string.
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN.

functions.name: MEM_mallocN_aligned
functions.signature: void *MEM_mallocN_aligned(size_t len, size_t alignment, const char *str);
functions.description: Allocates an uninitialized, alignment-constrained block of memory of size len bytes, tagged with str.
requirements: alignment specifies the desired alignment in bytes; must be a valid alignment supported by the implementation (exact constraints not specified here).
str must be a static string (only a pointer is stored).
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN (or appropriate aligned-aware free in the same allocator backend).

functions.name: MEM_malloc_arrayN_aligned
functions.signature: extern void *(*MEM_malloc_arrayN_aligned)(size_t len, size_t size, size_t alignment, const char *str);
functions.description: Function-pointer entry that allocates an uninitialized, alignment-constrained array (len elements of size bytes) with tracking tag/name str.
requirements: The product len * size must fit in size_t (implementation performs allocation for that total size).
alignment must be a valid alignment supported by the allocator.
str must be a static string (only a pointer is stored).
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN (in the same allocator backend).

functions.name: MEM_calloc_arrayN_aligned
functions.signature: extern void *(*MEM_calloc_arrayN_aligned)(size_t len, size_t size, size_t alignment, const char *str);
functions.description: Function-pointer entry that allocates a zero-initialized, alignment-constrained array (len elements of size bytes) with tracking tag/name str.
requirements: The product len * size must fit in size_t.
alignment must be a valid alignment supported by the allocator.
str must be a static string (only a pointer is stored).
Returned pointer must be freed with MEM_freeN (in the same allocator backend).

functions.name: MEM_printmemlist_pydict
functions.description: Function-pointer entry that prints all allocated blocks as a Python dict for inspection.
requirements: No arguments; may be null if the allocator backend does not provide it.

functions.name: MEM_printmemlist
functions.description: Function-pointer entry that prints a list of all allocated memory blocks (names and sizes).
requirements: No arguments; may be null if the allocator backend does not provide it.

functions.name: MEM_callbackmemlist
functions.description: Function-pointer entry that invokes the provided callback for every allocated memory block.
requirements: func must be a valid function pointer with signature void(void *).
The callback will be called for each allocated block; reentrancy or mutation within the callback should be considered carefully (unspecified here).

functions.name: MEM_printmemlist_stats
functions.description: Function-pointer entry that prints statistics about memory usage.
requirements: No arguments; may be null if the allocator backend does not provide it.

functions.name: MEM_set_error_callback
functions.description: Function-pointer entry to set a callback used for error output by the allocator.
requirements: func must be a valid function pointer taking a const char * message, or possibly NULL to clear (behavior of NULL not specified).

functions.name: MEM_consistency_check
functions.description: Function-pointer entry that verifies allocator guard markers and internal consistency.
requirements: Returns true if memory is consistent and false if corruption is detected.

functions.name: MEM_set_memory_debug
functions.description: Function-pointer entry to enable OS-level behavior to avoid zeroed malloc/stack (platform-specific; used primarily on macOS and similar).
requirements: No arguments; effect is platform/implementation-specific.

functions.name: MEM_get_memory_in_use
functions.description: Function-pointer entry returning the total number of bytes currently in use by the allocator.
requirements: No arguments; returns a size in bytes.

functions.name: MEM_get_memory_blocks_in_use
functions.description: Function-pointer entry returning the current number of allocated memory blocks.
requirements: No arguments; returns count of blocks.

functions.name: MEM_reset_peak_memory
functions.description: Function-pointer entry that resets the recorded peak memory usage to zero.
requirements: No arguments.

functions.name: MEM_get_peak_memory
functions.description: Function-pointer entry returning the peak memory usage in bytes, including mmap allocations.
requirements: No arguments; returns a size in bytes.

functions.name: MEM_name_ptr
functions.description: [Debug-only] Function-pointer entry that returns the debug name/tag currently associated with the given allocated block.
requirements: Only available when NDEBUG is not defined (debug builds).
vmemh must be a pointer previously allocated by this allocator.
Return value is a pointer to the stored static string, or possibly NULL if none (exact behavior unspecified).

functions.name: MEM_name_ptr_set
functions.description: [Debug-only] Function-pointer entry that changes the debug name/tag for the memory block at vmemh. Only affects the guarded allocator.
requirements: Only available when NDEBUG is not defined (debug builds).
vmemh must be a pointer previously allocated by this allocator.
str must be a static string (only a pointer is stored).

functions.name: MEM_init_memleak_detection
functions.description: Enables memory leak detection; when enabled, information about leaks will be printed on process exit. Should be called as early as possible in the program.
requirements: Call early in program startup to ensure leaks are tracked from the beginning.

functions.name: MEM_enable_fail_on_memleak
functions.description: Causes the process to exit with a failure code if leaks are detected at shutdown. Useful for automated tests.
requirements: Should be used in conjunction with MEM_init_memleak_detection to actually record leaks.

functions.name: MEM_use_lockfree_allocator
functions.description: Switches allocator to a fast mode with reduced tracking (no per-block names), keeping counters and total bytes. Intended for production/performance-sensitive use.
requirements: Must be called before any allocation happens in the process; switching after allocations have occurred is not allowed.

functions.name: MEM_use_guarded_allocator
functions.description: Switches allocator to the slow, fully-guarded mode with locks and per-block tracking for debugging and leak/introspection features.
requirements: Must be called before any allocation happens in the process; switching after allocations have occurred is not allowed.

functions.name: MEM_new
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename... Args> T *MEM_new(const char *allocation_name, Args &&...args);
functions.description: Allocates memory for an object of type T using the guarded allocator and constructs it in-place with the provided arguments. Must be destroyed with MEM_delete (or matching C++ delete overloads using this backend).
requirements: allocation_name is a tag/name for tracking; recommended to be a static string.
Returned pointer must be deleted with MEM_delete (not MEM_freeN).
Do not assume zero-initialization; explicitly initialize members as needed.
May be used with any T constructible from Args...

functions.name: MEM_new_for_free
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename... Args> T *MEM_new_for_free(const char *allocation_name, Args &&...args);
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized storage for T (with alignment handling) and constructs T using default or provided arguments. Resulting object may be freed with either MEM_freeN (C-style) or MEM_delete. Intended for trivially copyable and destructible types managed by legacy C-style code.
requirements: T must be trivially copyable and trivially destructible (is_trivial_after_construction).
allocation_name is a tag/name for tracking; recommended to be a static string.
Safe to free with MEM_freeN or MEM_delete, but use exactly one of them once.
For alignof(T) > MEM_MIN_CPP_ALIGNMENT a memset(0) is used before construction.

functions.name: MEM_new_array_for_free
functions.signature: template <typename T> T *MEM_new_array_for_free(const size_t length, const char *allocation_name);
functions.description: Allocates storage for an array of length objects of type T with proper alignment, default-constructs each element, and returns the pointer. Designed for trivially destructible types managed by C-style code.
requirements: T must be trivially copyable and trivially destructible (is_trivial_after_construction).
length is the number of elements to allocate; each element is default-constructed.
allocation_name is a tag/name for tracking; recommended to be a static string.
Caller must release the memory with MEM_freeN (C-style) or a matching deallocator for the used backend; no automatic destruction of elements beyond trivial default construction.

functions.name: MEM_delete
functions.description: Destroys the object of type T pointed to by ptr and deallocates its memory via the guarded allocator. Supports polymorphic types by adjusting to the most derived address. Passing nullptr is allowed.
requirements: ptr must have been allocated with MEM_new or an operator new that uses MEM_guardedalloc as backend.
Do not pass pointers allocated by the C-style MEM_* allocation functions.
It is invalid to call MEM_delete on void*; cast to the correct T.
Passing nullptr is a no-op.

functions.name: MEM_construct_leak_detection_data
functions.description: Constructs a T managed by a shared_ptr, registers it internally so it survives until after leak detection runs, and returns a reference to it. Useful for holding global/static-like state that should not be reported as leaked.
requirements: Thread-safe call.
Do not let the returned object own memory allocated with MEM_* functions; such memory would be reported as leaked.
Keep user-level synchronization if multiple threads access the returned object.
